item.title: Hundreds protest in Valletta against Budget 2027 measures on third-country nationals
item.description: Hundreds of people marched through Valletta on Saturday evening in a "United Against Discrimination" protest against Budget 2027 measures that will place a financial burden on third-country nationals living and working in Malta. The march started at the Triton Fountain in Floriana and moved towards Parliament Square, where a concert protest featured live performances from six acts. Organisers estimated more than 1,000 people took part, with placards reading "we are people not numbers" and "dignity has no nationality". Groups behind the event, including TCNs United, TCN Alliance, Solidarjetà and Moviment Graffitti, say the measures are based on nationality and immigration status rather than service needs or tax contribution.

item.title: Four cars destroyed in Żabbar blaze; no injuries reported
item.description: Firefighters from station four brought a blaze that engulfed four vehicles in Żabbar under control on Saturday afternoon, the Civil Protection Department said. Crews arrived to find four internal combustion engine vehicles on fire and no one was injured. The Rapid Intervention Unit and 4PD, a medical team from Mater Dei Hospital's emergency department and Transport Malta officials assisted at the scene. Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield publicly thanked the Civil Protection Department.

item.title: Mercieca urges doctors to put patients first in testing dispute
item.description: The chair of the parliamentary health committee, Franco Mercieca, urged the Medical Association of Malta to prioritise patients and resolve concerns over new point-of-care testing equipment in health centres through dialogue rather than industrial action. The MAM registered a dispute with Primary Health Care Management in August, warning the equipment could delay treatment and lengthen waiting times. Health Minister Ian Borg has said the rollout will go ahead despite the objections.

item.title: Man breached bail conditions after removing electronic tag, court told
item.description: A 22-year-old man from Żabbar was remanded for four days after the court heard that he breached the conditions of his bail by removing his electronic monitoring tag. The accused had been arrested on 11 November on charges of domestic violence and a breach of provisional liberty conditions, and was ordered to wear the device. Police received four reports, three stating he was out of his home when he should have been locked in. The defence asked for bail with a Caritas condition; the case was adjourned to next Thursday.

item.title: Government targets 2,000 specialised gaming jobs by 2035 as PLAYCON opens
item.description: GamingMalta's sixth PLAYCON edition opened at the weekend, with a Labour delegation including Minister Rosianne Cutajar, MEP Daniel Attard and MP Clint Azzopardi Flores touring the event. Government targets include more than 2,000 specialised jobs and at least 35 game development studios by 2035, with the sector expected to contribute 1% to 2% of Gross Value Added. Support schemes include a €200,000 Video Game Gateway Fund and a €2 million Video Game Production Rebate.

item.title: Veteran Maltese broadcaster Eddie Darmanin dies aged 88
item.description: Veteran Maltese broadcaster Eddie Darmanin, known for a long career across Rediffusion, RTK and Radio Malta, died on 21 November at the age of 88. Born in Isla in 1938 as the eldest of six siblings, he began work with International Aeradio Limited as a communication officer in the airport control tower at Hal Luqa, where he was involved in communications during the 1973 and 1985 aircraft hijackings. His broadcasting career began at Rediffusion and continued on RTK and Radio Malta.

item.title: MaltaToday survey: Budget bounce puts Labour four points ahead
item.description: A MaltaToday survey carried out after the budget found the Labour Party leading the Nationalist Party by 4.2 points, with 50% of the vote against 45.8%. The poll, run on 847 respondents between 4 and 19 November with a margin of error of ±3.4 points, puts Robert Abela's trust rating at 44.4% versus 36.2% for Alex Borg, and rates government performance at 3.2 out of 5. Some 80.8% of respondents said they would vote in an election now, up from 76% in October.
